analysis.one_liner: Freezes the minimum wage for temporary farm workers for 2022.
analysis.headline: The bill to freeze farm guest workers' minimum wages was introduced in the House in November 2021, sent to the Judiciary Committee, and died there without a hearing, markup, or vote.
analysis.plain_summary: The bill would stop a planned 2022 increase in the minimum wage the government sets for H-2A visa farm workers — the wage rate that is supposed to make sure foreign farm labor doesn't undercut domestic workers. It would apply in states with low unemployment or in states where food prices rose and the governor asked for the freeze. Farmers would pay their workers roughly $0.16 less an hour than under the scheduled increase. The bill was referred to the House Judiciary Committee and never got a hearing or a vote before the term ended.
analysis.who_benefits: Farm employers who use the H-2A guest worker program would save on wages for every hour worked by each guest worker. In states with low unemployment or rising food prices where a governor requests the freeze, they would avoid the scheduled 2022 wage increase. The bill is framed as a food-price relief, but any saving at the grocery store would depend on farmers passing it through rather than keeping it.
analysis.who_benefits_short: Farm employers using guest worker visas

how_it_helps.text: It freezes the H-2A adverse effect wage rate at its October 1, 2021 level through December 31, 2022 in states with unemployment at or below 5 percent, or in states where food prices rose more than 3 percent from December 2020 to September 2021 and the governor asks for the freeze.
The stated purpose is to stabilize food prices, on the theory that holding down farm labor costs keeps food from getting more expensive.

analysis.who_pays: H-2A farm workers, who would earn the 2021 minimum wage instead of the scheduled 2022 increase for work through the end of 2022. Any freeze also removes the pressure that higher guest-worker wages place on wages offered to U.S. farm workers.
analysis.who_pays_short: H-2A farm workers and U.S. farm workers

drawbacks.text: The adverse effect wage rate exists to protect U.S. and foreign farm workers from having their pay driven down; freezing it means the roughly $0.16-an-hour 2022 increase for covered workers would not happen.
The bill does not require any employer to pass savings on to consumers, so there is no mechanism guaranteeing it would actually lower grocery prices.

analysis.benefit_vs_cost: For farm employers, the bill would be a direct cost saving. For farm workers, it is a direct wage loss — a freeze on the one legal mechanism protecting agricultural wages from eroding. The food-price argument is indirect and unenforceable in the bill text.

outcome.mechanism: It was referred to the House Judiciary Committee on November 4, 2021 and to a subcommittee a year later, and never received a hearing or a vote before the Congress ended.

narrative.text: Introduced November 4, 2021, and referred to the House Judiciary Committee the same day.
On November 1, 2022 — a year later and just before the term ended — it was referred to the Subcommittee on Immigration and Citizenship, the last action on record.
No hearing, markup, or floor vote is recorded.

outcome.who_came_out_ahead: Farm employers who use the H-2A program benefit from the bill never advancing: they avoided no cost from it passing, but also faced no new obligation; the main gain is that the scheduled 2022 wage increase for farm workers went into effect rather than being frozen at 2021 levels. Farm workers came out ahead relative to where they would have been under this bill.

analysis.who_came_out_ahead_short: Farm workers and farm employers, in different ways

for.name: W. Gregory Steube
for.what_they_did: Introduced the bill to freeze the H-2A adverse effect wage rate through 2022.

sides.party_line_note: The sponsor and all 19 cosponsors were Republicans; no Democrat supported it. The bill died in committee without opposition ever being formally recorded.

industries.industry: Farm employers using the H-2A guest worker program
industries.note: They stood to pay less per hour for H-2A labor if the wage increase were frozen. The bill was drafted for their benefit, but since it died without action, nothing changed in practice.
